To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Alpha-lactalbumins are present in a wide variety of tissues, and in many of these they are associated with the galactosyltransferase in a manner that is analogous to the complex formed in the mammary tissue.
alpha-lactalbumins are present in the male reproductive tract and may be important in the synthesis of glycoproteins and/or the regulation of glycoprotein metabolism in these tissues.

The male reproductive tract contains a protein with a primary structure that is similar to alpha‐lactalbuminand that this protein is a component of a lactose synthetize complex that is similar in its properties to the complex of the mammary gland.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation, purification and characterization of alpha-lactalbumins, or alpha-lactalbuminalike proteins from the male reproductive tract.
the identification of proteins in the male reproductive tract which have properties similar to the lactose synthase proteins.
the isolation, characterization and synthesis of alpha‐lactalbumins from various species and with the elucidation of the role(s) of these proteins in the male reproductive tract.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

alpha-lactalbumins are a family of small proteins that have the ability to modify the substrate specificity of a ubiquitous galactose transferase in the mammary glands of all mammals and in the male reproductive tract of some species of mammals, and that they have no other known biological functions.
alpha-lactalbumins are proteins that are able to modify galactosyl-transferases by forming complexes with them.
the lactose synthase complex is a unique enzyme which catalyzes the synthesis of lactose by a reaction which is normally catalyzed by a different enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that alpha-lactalbumins are produced in a variety of tissues, including the male reproductive tract and that these proteins may function as modulators or modifiers of other enzymes in the manner of the mammary gland enzyme.

we have found alpha-lactalbumins in the testes, epididymides and prostate glands of several species and that these are similar to, and may have the same function as, alpha-lactaalbumin in the mammary glands of lactating mammals.
alpha-lactalbumins are a family of proteins which share a common structure and are found in the male reproductive tract.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use a protein to control an enzymatic reaction that is not normally controlled by a protein.
we can use this information to help us design better drugs.
alpha-lactalbumins are not just found in the mammary glands.
